answer: One concrete mechanism: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because thread only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, river is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any ember approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
